we synthesized new structural models for water oxidizing complex of Photosytem II, which can be used for artificial photosyntheic systems.
the compounds may represent the initial steps to synthesize a guanidinium/imidazole/manganese hybrid as a biomimetric system for the water oxidizing complex of Photosystems II.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a hybrid system that can mimic the structure of the manganese oxide cluster of the water-oxidising complex of Photosystem II and can be used as a structural model of this complex.
the development of new structural models for water oxidation in artificial photosynthetic water oxidation systems.
the design and development of new structural models for Photosystem II.

these compounds are promising structural models for the design of a hybrid of guandidinium or imadizolium together with manganese oxide for the water- oxidizing complex of Photosystems II.
the synthesized compounds are a good model of the structure of the water-oxidation complex of Photosystem II.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the compounds synthesized in this study are promising models for the water oxidation system of Photosystem II.
the guanidinium- and imidazoline-based manganese oxide monosheet hybrids may be promising candidates for the design and synthesis of artificial photosynthetic materials.
manganese oxide monosheet self-assembled with guanidinium (or imidazole) can be used to model the water-oxidating complex of Photosystem II.

the hybrid of guanidine or imidazole and manganese may serve as a promising structural analogue for the water- oxidizing complex of Photosysten II.
the hybrid of guanidine or imidazole with manganese oxide may represent a new approach for biomimetic water splitting.
we have synthesized and characterized a new class of compounds, which are promising structural models for the design of biomimetic systems for the water- oxidizing complex of Photosystems II.
